levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: An assumption is named but it is not one the conclusion actually depends on.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: A load-bearing assumption is named and its effect on the conclusion is stated.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: A load-bearing assumption is named, tested against the scenario, and bounded.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The conclusion is stated as certain when the scenario does not support that.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: Uncertainty is mentioned in general terms only.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The response says what is not known and how it limits the conclusion.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The response says what is not known, how it limits the conclusion, and what would resolve it.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: The parts of the plan contradict each other or do not add up.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up but one part is not connected to the rest.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up and each part is consistent with the others and with the constraint.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The plan adds up, is internally consistent, and states what would break it first.

levels.label: Not yet
levels.descriptor: A choice is asserted with no cost acknowledged.

levels.label: Approaching
levels.descriptor: A choice is defended but what it gives up is not named.

levels.label: Meets
levels.descriptor: The choice is defended and what it costs or forecloses is named specifically.

levels.label: Exceeds
levels.descriptor: The choice is defended, its cost is named, and the strongest case against it is answered.

judgment.prompt: Insuring costs $179.00 a year more in expected terms and is still the right choice here. Explain what the household is buying with that $179.00, and state the general condition under which self-insuring is the better option.
acceptableAnswerCriteria: Explains that the $179.00 buys the removal of an outcome the household cannot survive: a $4,200 loss against a $1,500 reserve.
States the general condition: self-insuring is better when the reserve can absorb the largest plausible loss without disrupting the rest of the plan.
Recognises that an insurer must charge more than the expected loss, so paying more than the expectation is the normal case rather than a sign of a bad policy.
evidenceRequirements: Cites the $252.00 expected loss, the $431.00 expected cost with the policy, and the $2,700.00 reserve shortfall.
lookFors: The response identifies capacity to absorb the loss as the deciding factor, not the expected cost.
The response explains why the premium exceeds the expected loss rather than treating it as overcharging.
A response noting that the household could self-insure once the reserve passes about $4,200 is stating the condition correctly.
judgment.commonMisconception: Choosing between insuring and self-insuring on expected cost alone.

evidenceRequirements: Refers to the 15.1-year figure and to the $179.00 annual saving it is built from.
